  content updates.
- **IoT prototype (ESP8266 / Arduino):** from ₹2,999, components billed at cost.
- Every project gets a fixed written quote first. Typical business website is
  live in 1–2 weeks. Works remotely with clients in Kerala, the rest of India
  and abroad.

## Projects

- [ExamForge](https://github.com/pranav-pradeesh/ExamForge): Mock-exam platform for JEE and VIT. A full-screen timed test engine (question
  palette, flagging, per-question timing, auto-submit), AI post-exam analysis and
  explanations through the Groq API, and an admin panel for the question bank.
  Next.js 14, TypeScript, Supabase (PostgreSQL with row-level security).
- [Gas Guard](https://github.com/pranav-pradeesh/GAS-GUARD): ESP8266 (NodeMCU) gas-leak detector in C++. Calibrates an MQ2 sensor at boot,
  then on a leak sounds a buzzer, opens a servo-driven vent and sends a Blynk
  alert. Serves its own web dashboard, falls back to an access point when Wi-Fi is
  down, and supports over-the-air updates.
- [NMHSS Thirunavaya](https://github.com/pranav-pradeesh/nmhss-project): The official website for his school, live and in daily use. Built by a team of
  two: Pranav built the frontend (React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vite) —
  public pages and the admin screens staff use to publish news, events and
  gallery media — working with a backend developer on the Express API.
- [Orvaya](https://github.com/pranav-pradeesh/Orvaya): Client work — a responsive
  marketing website built for a real business.

## Stack

- **Languages:** C++, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS
- **Web:** React, Next.js, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL (Supabase), MongoDB,
  Tailwind CSS, Three.js
- **IoT / systems:** ESP8266, Arduino, sensors and actuators, Blynk, Linux, Git
- **How he works:** AI-assisted development, rapid prototyping, version control
  with Git, learning from official documentation

## Questions and answers

**Who is Pranav Pradeesh?**
A first-year B.Tech Computer Science student at NCERC Pambady in Kerala, India,
who started coding at 12 and builds web,
IoT and backend projects, most of them started to understand how something works.

**What has he built?**
Four shipped projects: ExamForge (mock-exam platform with AI feedback), Gas
Guard (ESP8266 gas-leak detector), the frontend of the NMHSS Thirunavaya school
website (live in production), and Orvaya (a client website).

**What technologies does he use?**
C++, Python, JavaScript and TypeScript; React, Next.js, Node.js, Express,
PostgreSQL (Supabase), MongoDB, Tailwind CSS and Three.js on the web; ESP8266,
Arduino, sensors, Blynk, Linux and Git for IoT and systems work.

**Is he available for work?**
Yes — he is looking for an internship in web development, IoT or backend, where
he can contribute and learn from more experienced engineers.
He also takes small freelance web projects — see
https://pranavpradeesh.dev/services.

**How much does a website cost with Pranav Pradeesh?**
A small business website (up to 5 pages) starts at ₹4,999 with a fixed quote,
no monthly hosting fee for static sites, and the domain registered in the
client's name. Details: https://pranavpradeesh.dev/services.

**How do you contact him?**
Email pranavpradeesh09@gmail.com, via GitHub at
https://github.com/pranav-pradeesh, or on LinkedIn at
https://www.linkedin.com/in/pranav-pradeesh-9994a640b/.

**Where is he based?**
Kerala, India.

**Where does he study?**
First-year B.Tech Computer Science at Nehru College of Engineering and Research
Centre (NCERC), Pambady, Kerala, graduating in 2030. Before that, NMHSS
Thirunavaya — whose official website he built the frontend for, and which is
still live.

**What is ExamForge?**
A JEE and VIT mock-exam platform Pranav built in Next.js 14, TypeScript and
Supabase (PostgreSQL). It has a full-screen timed test engine with auto-submit,
AI post-exam analysis and question explanations through the Groq API, and an
admin panel for managing the question bank.

**What is Gas Guard?**
An ESP8266 IoT safety device written in C++. It reads an MQ2 gas sensor, and on
a leak sounds a buzzer, opens a servo-driven vent and sends a Blynk alert. It
also serves a local web dashboard that keeps working without internet.

**Has he shipped anything real users depend on?**
Yes — the NMHSS Thirunavaya school website, whose frontend he built, is live in
production and in daily use by the school. Orvaya is a website built for a paying business client.

**How long has he been coding?**
Since the age of 12.

**What kind of internship is he looking for?**
Web development, IoT or backend. He is looking for a team where he can contribute
real work and learn from more experienced engineers.

**How does he work?**
He uses AI-assisted development to move faster, and makes sure he can explain
every line he ships — how the data flows, where it can break, and why it is
built that way. Most projects start from wanting to understand how something
works.

**Topics and technologies**
student developer, web development, backend development, IoT, embedded systems,
C++, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, React, Next.js, Node.js,
Express, PostgreSQL, Supabase, MongoDB, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, ESP8266,
Arduino, Blynk, sensors, Linux, Git, AI-assisted development, Kerala, India,
software internship
